newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bank PBK sale could come next week-adviser.
newsitem.headline: Polish bank PBK sale could come next week-adviser.

text.p: The Polish Finance Ministry could decide on an investor for up to 65 percent of Polski Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK) in the next few days, an official from the ministry's adviser on the sale, HSBC Investment Services, said.
"I hope to get the decision on Monday or Tuesday next week, but that's my hope as an adviser," HSBC's Hubert Janiszewski told a news conference on Thursday.
In January the finance ministry invited bids for no less than 10 percent and no more than 65 percent of PBK, with an initial public offer for another 15 percent likely in October. @

Janiszewski would not say how many entities had been shortlisted in the tender for the bank which his firm has estimated as having a total value of between 1.2 billion and 1.6 billion zlotys. A consortium of Polish Development Bank (PBR), Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy (BPH), Kredyt Bank and insurer Warta has said it submitted a bid for a 51-percent stake in PBK. @
Banking sources have said Citibank and South Korea's Samsung were also interested in buying stakes in PBK but neither confirmed the report. -- Steven Silber +48 22 653 9700
